title: Seller Rapid Trust Sprint Cards (annotated draft)
body:
Deck purpose: ultra-compact, conversation-first slide set + one-page battlecards for quick trust-building with platform engineers and SREs during pilot day 0. Not a full training pack — this is what to hand to an engineer in the room and to leave as a single-sheet follow-up.

Structure (6 slides + appendix):
- 1: 90s opener (what teams we help, blunt econ and reliability bullets)
- 2: 3 micro-scenarios (Embedding search, Chat assistant, Reranking) with quick metrics and fallbacks
- 3: Fallback matrix (model variants, quantization tiers, region failover) + one-liner scripts
- 4: Integration checklist (proxy, auth, prefix cache + sample curl snippets)
- 5: Cost/latency cheat sheet (how to run a 10k-token/day pilot and estimate committed spend)
- 6: 2-minute demo script (what SE should say, what to show)
- Appendix: two battlecards (Engineer-facing and Exec-facing) + quick SDK snippet samples

Slide 1 notes (90s opener):
- 30s tagline: "Same inference everywhere — hosted, reserved, private — with production SLOs you can measure."
- 30s econ: "Pilot baseline: 10k tokens/day typical P0 for feature proof; expect 8-12% latency reduction with caching and 30-45% token-cost reduction with prefix reuse + model routing."
- 30s reliability: "Canary, A/B, automatic fallback to cheaper quantized variant. SLA/uptime: option for Dedicated customers."

Micro-scenarios (slide 2):
- Embedding search (retail catalog): target p95 < 120ms for 1–4k concurrent lookups; technique: local embedding cache + batched embedder endpoint; fallback: async batch-update with degraded freshness.
- Chat support assistant (customer care): target p50 < 50ms token generation for short prompts; technique: streaming + KV cache; fallback: strict truncation + shorter context model variant.
- Reranking for recommendations: throughput-first; target 200–500 qps for rerank loop; technique: dedicated pool with optimized kernels + quantized reranker; fallback: linear-reranker CPU-only with cached features.

Fallback matrix (slide 3):
- Columns: problem | short-term stopgap | medium-term fix | what to promise the customer
- Examples: model OOM -> route to lower-seq model variant; sudden QPS spike -> burst to reserved pool or region fallback; unacceptable latency -> enable prefix cache and reduce max tokens.
- Seller one-liners to use: "If latency spikes, we’ll automatically route to a compatible lower-memory variant and keep responses flowing while we investigate."

Integration checklist (slide 4):
- Preflight: CORS / allowed origins, API key perms, VPC peering request form (link in appendix)
- Instrumentation: add header X-Redwood-Trace: {{trace-id}} for correlation (example curl in appendix)
- Pilot routing: set tag pilot=true, route to dedicated pilot pool if available
- Security: if Private, confirm KMS key id and audit log ship destination
- Quick curl snippet (engineer-friendly):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \n    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n    -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-1","input":"<prompt>","metadata":{"pilot":"acct-123"}}'

Cost & latency cheat sheet (slide 5):
- Pilot sizing rule-of-thumb: 10k tokens/day -> < $200/mo hosted; 100k tokens/day -> consider reserved for predictability
- Quick math examples: 
  - Short chat (avg 60 tokens/response) at 2k/day responses -> 120k tokens/day -> hosted cost estimate = token_rate * 120k -> show model-specific per-token numbers during handoff
  - Embedding cache: storing top 50k vectors in-memory reduces embed calls by ~85% in early pilot tests
- Observable knobs sellers should mention: batch_window_ms, max_tokens, quantize=true/false

2-minute demo script (slide 6):
- 0:00–0:20: Intro — "We’ll run two calls: a chat flow and an embedding call (search). I’ll show you latency, then toggle caching and show improvement."
- 0:20–1:00: Run baseline chat, show p95 in console and token count cost; note logs in trace.
- 1:00–1:40: Flip on prefix cache in Console or API header, re-run; highlight p95 drop and cost delta.
- 1:40–2:00: Show fallback demo: force a large input / OOM and show auto-fallback to variant with same API surface.

Appendix: battlecards (two 1-pagers)
- Engineer-facing battlecard (one pager):
  - Quick wins to reduce latency: enable streaming, prefix cache, lower max_tokens, route to dedicated pool for high qps
  - When to escalate to Redwood SRE: persistent p95 > 300ms after caching/batching enabled, memory errors, or unknown error codes 5xx happening in > 1% of requests
  - Useful debug headers: X-Redwood-Model, X-Redwood-Variant, X-Redwood-Trace
  - Links: Confluence pilot runbook, GitHub sample app repo, Jira triage board

- Exec-facing battlecard (one pager):
  - One-liner value: "Reduce inference cost friction and keep your feature available under load — predictable economics and rollback policy included."
  - Top buying signals: spikes in cost to serve, need for private deployment, audit/compliance requirements
  - Risk narrative: explain graceful degradation — what users will see: slightly shorter/less detailed responses, no full outage

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Pull recent pilot numbers from analytics team (JIRA GTMINF-1428) and replace the placeholder cost examples before wider distribution.
- Add region fallback flow visual (need SRE diagram).
- Ask SEs on rotation for 2–3 real quotes to include in exec battlecard.

Hand-off checklist before field push:
- Replace placeholder numbers with real metrics (owner: Priya)
- Run deck with two SEs in 30-min dry run and capture pushback
- Publish to Confluence as living doc and link to sample app repo

Slack snippets for sellers to use (short copy):
- For engineers: "Quick test idea: enable X-Redwood-PrefixCache and run the same prompt — you should see p95 drop by ~X ms and token cost fall."
- For procurement/exec: "We can start with a small reserved pilot to cap spend and enable fast fallback routing — happy to share a one-page pilot commitment."

Version history: draft v0.7 — created 2025-11-12 by Marcus Li; edits 2026-02-20: updated demo script and added router-one-liners.

Notes: keep language prescriptive and engineer-first; this deck should be printable as two slides per page for handouts at pilot kickoff. Replace all placeholders before finalization.
